answers.explanation: The OS sits between users (and their programs) and the hardware. A compiler translates code, and it's an application, not the OS.
The OS sits between them. Programs ask the OS to read files, draw windows, or send packets, and the OS drives the hardware.
The three goals are executing programs, convenience, and efficiency. Programs take as long as their work needs.
Users can be people, machines, or other computers: whoever wants work done.
Application programs define how the system's resources are used to solve users' problems.
A server answering requests from other machines has computers as its users.
Hardware provides the basic computing resources the rest of the system shares.
That's the OS's whole job: coordinating shared hardware.
